name: std_PrintfFormatInt
signature: void std_PrintfFormatInt(PrintfStream* out, int conv, s64 value)
summary: Emits one integer conversion for printf: writes the decimal digits of the 64-bit value into the stream buffer at out+0x24, chooses the sign prefix from the stream flags (minus / plus / space) and hands it to the padding writer. Used by the %d/%i/%u family; conv == 0xf5 skips sign handling.
evidence: Stream layout matches the CRT printf state: [0]=flags (bit1 = negative, bit2 = plus), [4]=putc callback, [0x18]=field width, [0x1c]=precision, [0x20]=chars written, +0x24=digit buffer. Tail call to std_PrintfEmitPadded (0x002FF7C4); digit loop calls 0x002FF874 (u64 divide by 10); sign strings "-" "+" " " live at 0x0010045C/0x00100460/0x00100464.

name: std_SetErrno
summary: Stores err into the C library errno cell. Called by the soft-float and libm routines when they detect a domain/range error, so the value is what the caller sees in errno afterwards.
evidence: func_002FF9C4 returns the address of the per-process errno word (ldr r0,[pc,#0] -> 0x007F3020); this wrapper just does *errno_location() = arg1. 11 callers, all math/format helpers (sqrt, atan family, printf float formatting).

name: std_StrtofCore
signature: float std_StrtofCore(FloatResult* result, const char* digits, const char* exponent, int exp2)
summary: Turns the already-scanned decimal digit string plus its decimal exponent into a float: builds the 64-bit mantissa, normalises it, scales by the power of ten, applies the current rounding mode and stores the 32-bit result, setting ERANGE when the value overflows.
evidence: Called only from std_Strtod (0x00101314). Digit strings are 0xff terminated; sign/exponent computed with a shift-subtract loop; uses 0x002FFDC0 (rounding mode), 0x00126848/0x00126878 (double mul/div by 10^k), 0x00300D50 (double->float narrowing). Result is a 2-word struct (value + status) exactly like the RVCT strtod worker.

name: std_Strtod
signature: double std_Strtod(const char* text, char** end, int* status, ScanCtx* ctx)
summary: The C library strtod: reads sign, digits, decimal separator (from the locale block), "0x" hex floats and an exponent through the ctx getc/ungetc callbacks and returns the parsed double, updating the end pointer and the conversion status.
evidence: Uses ctx callbacks at +0x18/+0x20/+0x1c/+0x10 (getc, peek, ungetc, locale); accepts i/n (inf/nan), 0x (calls 0x001015D8 hex path), decimal point from locale block (*ctx[0])->+0xc; ends in std_StrtofCore/std_DoubleConvert. Only caller 0x00300714 is the scanf float handler.

name: std_ParseHexFloat
signature: int std_ParseHexFloat(char* buf, char** end, u16* out, ScanCtx* ctx, int pos, u32 flags, int len)
summary: Parses the significand of a hexadecimal float literal ("0x1.8p3") into a double and applies the binary exponent; returns the number of characters consumed or -2 on a malformed literal.
evidence: Collects up to 16 mantissa nibbles with func_003006F0(ch,16) (digit value), keeps a 6-bit shift counter, handles "p"/"P" binary exponents with +/- and calls 0x006B8138 (ldexp) plus the rounding mode from 0x002FFDC0. Reached from strtod through the 0x001015D8 alias.

name: maybe_Pack_GetManager
summary: Returns (through out) the lazily created global pack/resource manager: an array of 0x220-byte manager objects, one per registered pack slot, whose first element gets a vtable installed at creation time. Every pack load goes through the pointer this returns.
evidence: First-call-only init flag 0x007BE32C, cached pointer 0x007BE330, slot count 0x00833D28, vtable 0x007829E0 installed by 0x00122120. Callers do func_00388320(*mgr, 1, "s_gamecmn.pack") and func_003882F0(out, *mgr, id, buf) i.e. register/lookup a pack. 43 callers.

name: std_DoubleDivide
signature: void std_DoubleDivide(const double* lhs, const double* rhs, int mode, double* out)
summary: Soft-float double divide wrapper: if both operands are finite normal numbers it runs the mantissa divide core (exponent subtraction) and returns the packed double; special values are left to the caller.
evidence: Checks (a[1] & ~(a[0]<<1)) < 0 for both operands = exponent neither 0 nor 0x7ff, then calls 0x001263C8 (mantissa divide: subtracts exponent fields) and 0x00126710 (pack/return). Used by std_StrtofCore to scale by a negative power of ten.

name: std_DoubleMultiply
signature: void std_DoubleMultiply(const double* lhs, const double* rhs, int mode, double* out)
summary: Soft-float double multiply wrapper: for two finite normal operands it runs the mantissa multiply core (exponent addition) and returns the packed double.
evidence: Same shape as 0x00126848 but tests bit 0x40000000 (non-zero significand) and calls 0x001268A8, which adds the exponent fields (`add r3,r7,ip; sub r3,r3,#0x3f00`). Used by std_StrtofCore for a positive decimal exponent.

name: Script_ReportParseError
signature: void Script_ReportParseError(void* vm, const char* source, int line, int column, const char* message)
summary: Reports a Squirrel script compile/parse error in the standard form "%s line = (%d) column = (%d) : error %s" using the printer installed in the script VM.
evidence: Format string at 0x0015C774 = "%s line = (%d) column = (%d) : error %s\n"; printer obtained from 0x006BBBE4 (script VM accessor) and invoked with the five arguments. Sits in the script-native block next to SetMessageArgItemName / SetupLocatorFromActor.

The block at 0x0015EC8C is ARM: bl 0x0044C3D0 (handle->object table lookup, key = handle>>11), if null -> return 1, else bl 0x0064E130 = ldrsb [obj+0x2B4]. The Ghidra readable C for this address (thumb float math) is a misdecompilation.

name: Field_IsPointInActorViewCone
signature: u32 Field_IsPointInActorViewCone(Actor* self, float* point, int allowHeightCheck, int scaleRadius)

name: std_DivideU64
summary: Unsigned 64-bit divided by 10 with the remainder returned in the high word: the shift/add division sequence used by the itoa/printf digit loops to peel one decimal digit per call.

name: std_ScaleByPowerOfTen

summary: Multiplies/divides a double by 10^exponent by splitting the exponent into base-55 chunks and using a table of pre-scaled 10^k constants, i.e. the power-of-ten scaling step of strtod/dtoa.
evidence: Splits exponent with func_0011CD80(n+0x1B9B, 0x37) (n/55), walks the 16-byte 10^k table at 0x002FFE50/0x002FFDD4 and combines the parts with 0x002FFEC8 (double multiply) and 0x002FFE98 (divide); callers 0x00101100 (strtof core) and 0x002FFEFA (dtoa).

evidence: Calls 0x001263C8 (divide core) then 0x0012676C (pack, register variant of 0x00126710). Used by 0x002FFDC8 and 0x002FFEFA.

name: std_DoubleToDecimal

summary: Converts a double to a decimal digit string for printf %e/%f/%g: scales by powers of ten until the digit count fits, emits digits (reversing them), trims leading zeros or rounds up one digit and reports the decimal point position plus the final digit count through result.

summary: Advances one animation/effect clock by delta: saves the previous value at +8, keeps the new value inside [0, limit] when the limit's wrap flag is clear, or wraps it modulo the limit with fmodf when the flag is set. This is the shared clock advance used by the scene/timeline objects in the 0x55-0x5A range.
evidence: value+4 current, value+8 previous, limit+4 flag byte (bit 0 selects wrap), limit+8 upper bound; callees std_Fmodf 0x00673288 and 0x006731EC (floor-ish); callers 0x0057B0EC (Anim_UpdateBlendTracks), 0x005A95D0, 0x005A9990 plus the 3-instruction adapters 0x00564614 and 0x0055E61C which pass a sub-object's field and its own limit pointer.

name: Model_CalcLookAtAngles
signature: void Model_CalcLookAtAngles(LookAtController* self, Model* model, u32 unused, float* outYaw, float* outPitch)
summary: Computes the horizontal and vertical rotation ratios a model needs to face its look-at target: transforms the target into the model's space, projects the offset onto the horizontal and vertical planes, takes the acos of the normalised components and applies the controller's per-axis limits (+0x324/+0x328), smoothing (+0x32C/+0x330) and rate (+0x334).
evidence: Sole caller 0x0056BE48 (Model_UpdateLookAt) feeds the two ratios into the bone rotations; callees 0x005754C0 (transform reconstruction) and std_Acosf 0x00672A14; output is divided by the live-bone limit from g_0056BE44; self+0x32C/0x330 are the smoothed values and +0x334 the blend rate, mirrored by the constants g_0056BE38..BC.

name: Model_UpdateLookAt
signature: u32 Model_UpdateLookAt(LookAtController* self, Model* model, ModelBoneMatrices* bones)
summary: Applies head/body look-at: computes the target yaw/pitch ratios (or reuses the smoothed ones while the controller fades out), slerps each of the two affected bone rotations toward the computed target orientation with its own blend factor, converts them into 3x4 matrices in the bone table and returns 0 once the blend and angles have settled, 1 while look-at is still running.
evidence: Two-slot loop (i<2) writing 0x40-byte matrix records into bones+0xC at indices self+0x31C; sets flag bit 2 in the record's first word; callees 0x0056BC20 (angle ratios), 0x00672A14 acos and 0x00673BC8 sin/cos; enable flag +0x33D, 'reuse stored blend' flag +0x33E, rate +0x334; returns 0 when the weights fall below g_0056C22C. No direct C callers, so it is invoked through the model's look-at callback.

name: Math_QuatSlerp
signature: void Math_QuatSlerp(float* out, const float* q0, const float* q1, float t)
summary: Spherical linear interpolation of two unit quaternions: negates q1 when the dot product is negative (shortest arc), falls back to a normalised lerp when the quaternions are nearly parallel, otherwise blends with acos/sin and renormalises the result.
evidence: Callers 0x003CFFA8 and 0x004F8280 blend a model's start/end rotations (self+0x44 / self+0x54) during a turn; callees std_Acosf 0x00672A14 and 0x00673BC8 (sin); constant g_00575858 (0.0, used for the sign flip) and g_0057585C (cosine cutoff above which the lerp fallback is used); identical structure to the vec3 slerp 0x00575864.

name: Math_Vec3Slerp
signature: void Math_Vec3Slerp(float* out, const float* v0, const float* v1, float t)
summary: Spherical interpolation between two 3D direction vectors: normalised lerp when the directions are nearly parallel, otherwise acos/sin slerp, always producing a unit direction. Used wherever a direction has to change smoothly (animation pose blending at 0x002E465C, 0x00591490).
evidence: Callers Anim_InterpolatePose (0x002E465C), 0x003E8F84, 0x004406A8, 0x00441B24 and 0x00591490 (camera blend); the parallel case delegates to 0x005753BC (vec3 lerp), otherwise acos 0x00672A14 / sin 0x00673BC8; 3-component dot with epsilon g_00575974.

name: std_Acosf
summary: Single-precision arccosine: for |x| <= 0.5 returns pi/2 - x - x^3*P(x^2); for 0.5 < |x| <= 1 uses the half-angle identity acos(x) = 2*asin(sqrt((1-|x|)/2)) (and pi minus that for negative x); sets EDOM and returns NaN when |x| > 1 and x*2 is not NaN.
evidence: ARM disassembly 0x00672A14: exponent-range test on x<<1 ([2^-27,1]), vabs/1.0-x/*0.5, bl 0x006BDF48 (sqrtf), polynomial coefficients at 0x00672B24..0x00672B38 (1/6, 3/40, 5/112 ...), pi/2 halves at 0x00672B20 (1.5708008) + 0x00672B24 (0.000484) and pi at 0x00672B14/0x00672B18, EDOM via 0x00100C16. 69 callers, all angle/facing code (ActorSetTurnSpeed*, Actor_ClassifyDirection*, 0x00178DD0 view-cone test). Ghidra C is unusable (VFP registers unmodelled).

name: maybe_std_Ceilf
summary: Single-precision ceiling: |x| >= 2^23 is already integral so it is returned unchanged; for |x| < 1 returns 1.0 for positive x and -0.0 for negative x (0.0 for zero); otherwise adds one fraction unit and clears the fractional mantissa bits, i.e. rounds upward. NaN is passed through.
evidence: IMPORTANT: the listed address 0x00672DA0 is inside atan2f literal pool (values -1/3, 1/5, -1/7 at 0x672DA0/DA4/DA8, 2^32 and 2^-32 at 0x672DAC/DB0); the real entry is 0x00672DB4. There the ARM code does: e = exponent(x) - 127; if (e >= 23) return x; if (e < 0) return x>0 ? 1.0 : (x<0 ? -0.0 : x); mask = 0x007fffff >> e (pool 0x672E40); if (x & mask)==0 return x; if (x > 0) bits += 0x800000 >> e; bits &= ~mask; return bits. NaN handling: x + 0x7149F2CA (~8e29, pool 0x672E38) compares unordered and returns the original NaN. 22 real callers (0x0015F8DC, 0x001E388C, 0x003122F4, 0x00603D0C/18/5C..., 0x00644A6C, 0x0065DD34) all do `vmul/vcvt -> bl 0x672DB4 -> vcvt.u32.f32`, i.e. float-to-integer rounding. Named ceilf rather than roundf/floorf because of the |x|<1 -> 1.0/-0.0 and positive-only increment.

name: std_Cosf
summary: Single-precision cosine: reduces x by n*pi/2 using the round-to-nearest magic constant 2^23 and a three-part pi/2 (1.57031 + 0.000483751 + 7.54953e-08), then evaluates either the cosine kernel (1 - x^2/2 + x^4/24 ...) or the sine kernel and applies the quadrant sign from n mod 4. Returns +/-inf for huge arguments and NaN/EDOM for NaN.
evidence: ARM disassembly 0x00672E4C (real entry 0x00672E44: ldr r2,=0x7E921FB6; vmov r1,s0; then push): n = vcvt(x * 2/pi (0x3F22F983) +/- 0.5 (0x4B000000 magic)), quadrant = n&3, reduction constants 0x3FC90000/0x39FDA000/0x33A22000, cos coefficients -0.499999/0.0416563/-0.00135978, sin coefficients -0.166667/0.00833198/0.000194956; sign from (n&2); huge threshold 0x46490E49. Ghidra lists the entry at 0x672E4C, i.e. 8 bytes into the function (the two argument-setup instructions are missing from the C file).

name: std_Expf
summary: Single-precision exponential: n = round(x * 4/ln2), r = x - n*(ln2 split into 0.173279 + 7.98655e-06), evaluates 1 + r + r^2/2 + r^3/6 + r^4/24 and multiplies by 2^(n/4) taken from a four-entry table {1, 2^0.25, sqrt2, 2^0.75} plus hi/lo correction terms; the integer part is applied in two halves (2^(n/2) * 2^(n-n/2)) to avoid exponent overflow. Over/underflow sets ERANGE and returns +/-inf or 0/0.

name: std_Fmodf
summary: Single-precision floating remainder: fmod(x,y) = x - trunc(x/y)*y. Detects NaN operands and delegates to the soft-float remainder core, raises EDOM and returns NaN for fmod(inf,y), passes fmod(x,inf) = x through, and applies a one-step sign correction (result - copysign(|y|, result)) when the returned remainder sign disagrees with x.
evidence: ARM disassembly 0x00673288: |operand| > 0x7F800000 (NaN) test on both, bl 0x00723D80 (unanalysed RVCT soft-float helper region 0x6BE000-0x7C3000, exponent masks 0xFF000000/0x00FF0000), `vdiv s18/s18` + 0x00100C16(1) for the inf case, sign compare of x and result, then `vsub.f32 s0, s0, s1` with s1 = sign(result)|abs(y). Callers are all camera/scene float math (0x0051B158, 0x0051B6B8, 0x0052BA7C, 0x0053F62C, 0x00564620, 0x0057E9F4, 0x005BA074). remainderf would be the alternative reading.

name: maybe_std_ModfBlockA
summary: Not a real function: 0x6733C2 falls in the middle of the ARM instruction `strlt r3,[r0,#4]` at 0x6733C0 inside std_Modf (0x00673360). Ghidra created a 4-byte Thumb function here because the byte pattern 0x80B5 (Thumb `push {r7,lr}`) occurs in the ARM encoding; its C body is a misdecompiled byte-swap stub.
evidence: ARM disassembly of the container: 0x6733BC cmp r1,#0; 0x6733C0 strlt r3,[r0,#4]; 0x6733C4 strlt r4,[r0]; 0x6733C8 blt 0x673430 - predicate setup for the "exponent < 0" branch of modf (store signed zero integer part). functions_merged.jsonl claims mode=thumb for 0x6733C2; 0x6733C2 is not 4-byte aligned, so it cannot be an ARM entry and the Thumb reading produces the `rev`-style garbage seen in FUN_006733C2_006733c2.c.

name: maybe_std_ModfBlockB
summary: Not a real function either: 0x6733C6 is the continuation of std_Modf (0x00673360) after the predicated stores, covering the truncation/rounding of the fractional bits, the integer-part copy to *iptr and the `fraction = original - integral` return. Ghidra again saw a Thumb 0x80B5 push pattern (the second half of `strlt r4,[r0]`) and produced a bogus 0xA2-byte body.
evidence: ARM disassembly: 0x6733CC..0x67345C implements the tail of modf - mask 0x000FFFFF (pool 0x673464), bias 0xFFFFFC01 (0x673460), exponent > 0x33 -> integral, `bic` fractional bits, `vldr d0,[r0] / vldr d1,[sp] / vsub.f64 d0,d1,d0` = x - trunc(x) returned in d0 while the integral part is stored through iptr (r0). Ghidra reports mode=thumb and a byte-swap body for both 0x6733C2 and 0x6733C6: keep-as-block only.

name: std_Scalbn
summary: Multiplies *value by 2^exponent in place with C99 overflow/underflow handling: results that overflow become +/-infinity and results that underflow are flushed to signed zero, both with errno=ERANGE (2); NaN/inf inputs are left untouched. This is the scaling step of the C library's hexadecimal float parser.
evidence: Sole caller 0x001015E0 (std_ParseHexFloat) calls it with the assembled mantissa double and the binary exponent; the body tests the 11 exponent bits against 0x7FF, calls the soft-float scaling core 0x00723F8C, compares the result with the infinity constants g_006B8218/g_006B8220, sets errno through std_SetErrno(2) and builds the overflow value from g_006B8228*g_006B8228 while preserving the sign bit.

name: std_Sqrtf
summary: Single-precision square root using the VFP vsqrt instruction; sets EDOM when the argument is negative (or NaN) and returns the NaN produced by vsqrt.
evidence: Recovered C: sQRT = SQRT(in_s0) then a comparison against g_006BDF94 (+inf, used as the "unordered/negative" test) followed by func_00100C16(1) = errno = EDOM. Only caller in this batch is std_Acosf (0x00672A14), which calls 0x006BDF48, the same routine 4 bytes earlier.
